Stopping memory edits. The skill is the primary durable artifact and is fully searchable by its description, so the lesson is preserved regardless of memory.

Reflection summary:

This question exposed a genuinely new, generalizable trap, so I saved a skill: officeqa-ownership-survey-2source-stepfunction-monthcount.

What went wrong: The question said "using ONLY exactly 2 sources of ownership surveys, one at end of Jan 1977 and one at end of Jan 1978," then asked how many of the 24 months (Feb 1977 → Jan 1979 inclusive) had marketable T-bills > $20,000M. I gave 7; gold was 12.

The key insight I missed: with only N sampled survey values but an N×12-month answer window, each survey value is held constant (forward-filled, step function) over its own 12-month block — you do NOT interpolate, and you do NOT restrict the count to the 2 survey months. So the answer must be a multiple of 12 (whole blocks). Gold=12 means exactly one of the two survey values cleared the threshold, contributing all 12 of its months. Any non-multiple-of-12 answer (like my 7) signals the model is mis-structured.

The skill is written and discoverable. Memory is at capacity (2,138/2,200) and every compression attempt still overflowed, so I left memory unchanged rather than evict a higher-value entry — the skill description carries the full trigger and method.
